writeup.headline: Patterson-UTI rates Hold: strong share-price trend offset by a weak balance sheet and soft growth.
writeup.thesis: Patterson-UTI scores 49, a Hold, five points above the Sell line and 16 below Buy. The strongest support is the trend score of 80: the price is 19.9% above its 200-day average and 4.2% below its 52-week high, and the shares are up 67.6% from 12 months ago to 1 month ago, though they trail SPY by 5.4 pp over the last 126 trading days. Against that, the balance sheet scores just 18, with net debt at 5.81 times free cash flow and cash covering only 0.16 of debt. Growth scores 40: there is a TTM revenue decline of 6.4% and latest-quarter revenue growth of 0.6% year on year, although growth sped up by 12.7 pp from the previous quarter. Valuation scores 40: in absolute terms P/S is 1.0x and P/FCF is 27.0x, with FCF yield 1.3 pp below the 10-year Treasury yield; against its own history, P/S is more expensive than at 42 of the last 61 month-ends, while P/FCF is not comparable (negative in 15 of 61 month-ends) and EV/EBIT is not comparable (negative now and in 29 of 61 month-ends).
key_risks: Leverage: net debt is 5.81 times free cash flow and cash covers only 0.16 of debt.
Thin profitability: operating margin is -1.1% and EBIT is negative, so an FCF margin of 3.8% leaves little cushion.
Guidance calls for a 5-10% sequential decline in Drilling Products on Saudi weakness.
After a 67.6% run the shares sit 4.2% below their 52-week high, and P/S is more expensive than at 42 of the last 61 month-ends.
Exposure to U.S. rig counts and completion activity, which faced temporary sand constraints in Q3.
what_would_change: A drop of 5 points in the score would move the rating to Sell, for example if the trend score weakens from 80 or news turns negative.
Moving up 16 points to Buy would likely need better balance sheet and valuation scores, such as debt reduction from the guided free cash flow increase in 2027.
A return to positive TTM revenue growth and a positive operating margin would lift the growth and quality scores.
